title.narrative: Winter Resilience: Strengthening Affected Communities and Local Population in Kharkiv, Donetsk, and Mykolaiv Regions

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to enhance the resilience and well-being of vulnerable communities in Kharkiv, Donetsk, and Mykolaiv oblasts by ensuring access to essential winter energy resources and providing financial assistance for utility expenses. This effort will reduce the risk of energy poverty and improve living conditions during the winter months.ltbrgtHelp seeks to support vulnerable communities in these regions by addressing critical winter energy needs with two activities: 1) the Winter Energy Activity, which provides solid fuel, and 2) the Winter Cash for Utilities Activity, providing cash assistance for utility expenses. The project will support the following categories of vulnerability: persons with disabilities (PwD), single parents, large families, and elderly people, with an emphasis on PwD. The project will emphasize localization by partnering with the local NGO Avalyst, ensuring that activities are carried out effectively and sustainably within the community.ltbrgtHelp's employees will lead the Winter Energy activity, distributing solid fuel to ensure that households have the necessary resources to stay warm during the harsh winter months. Vulnerable households will be identified through applications obtained from local self-government bodies, including the aid recipient's address. Previously, Help delivered solid fuel to central distribution points, incurring additional expenses for beneficiaries. Now, aid will be delivered directly to each household, ensuring timely and efficient support without extra expenses. Help representatives will procure solid fuel (3.5 tons of briquettes per household, in accordance with Shelter Cluster recommendations) and deliver it to the specified addresses. A total of 1,145 vulnerable households will receive in-kind solid fuel support. Help staff will monitor and assist at every stage. This activity will mitigate the risk of energy poverty and improve the living conditions of the most vulnerable populations in the targeted oblasts. ltbrgtIn collaboration with NGO Avalyst, the organization will also carry out the Winter Cash for Utilities activity by providing cash assistance to cover utility expenses. The partner organization will register and distribute financial assistance in the Kramatorsk and Pokrovsk raions of Donetsk oblast, according to the specified categories of vulnerability. Meetings will be announced through local authorities to register people with the relevant categories of vulnerability in various settlements of the community. After collecting and processing the data, funds will be transferred to help beneficiaries partially cover their winter utility expenses. Depending on the type of heating, there will be three different categories of payments: Cash for electricity - $453.60 per household, Cash for centralized gas - $368 per household, and Cash for centralized heating - $289.50 per household. Thus, 2,750 vulnerable households in the Kramatorsk and Pokrovsk raions will be supported. ltbrgtThis approach will enable households to manage their energy needs more flexibly and efficiently, alleviating financial stress and fostering economic stability within the community. The project will begin on September 1, 2024, and conclude on February 28, 2025, ensuring that both activities are completed before the critical winter period to maximize the impact and reach of the assistance provided. By leveraging local partnerships and addressing the community's urgent needs, this project aims to provide immediate relief and strengthen the long-term resilience of the affected populations.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
